name: LIBYA

flag.title: Libya's Flag
flag.note: Red, black & green with crescent & star

lead: Libya is a huge North African country where the Sahara meets the Mediterranean. More than 90% is desert, with golden dunes, black craters, and hidden lakes. It also has giant Roman ruins and huge oil fields.
geo: Libya's coast runs 1,770 km along the Mediterranean. Behind it, the land rises to high flat ground, then drops into the Sahara, the world's biggest hot desert.
In the southern Fezzan, hidden lakes shimmer among red dunes at Ubari. Rainwater trapped underground for thousands of years feeds them.
animals: The fennec fox's huge ears work like satellite dishes. They hear insects moving underground at night. It never needs to drink.
Barbary sheep scramble up rocky cliffs. Dorcas gazelles sprint over open sand. Sandfish skinks (lizards) 'swim' through loose sand and vanish in a blink.
culture: Bazin is Libya's national dish. Cooks boil firm bread dough in salted water. Couscous and spiced lamb appear at celebrations.
Berber families, an ancient North African people, have woven carpets and hammered silver for centuries. Shape patterns in every knot tell family stories.
history: Phoenician sea traders founded coastal cities around 1000 BC. Greeks settled Cyrene in 631 BC. Then Rome took over. Emperor Septimius Severus, born in Libya, rebuilt Leptis Magna into one of the grandest cities on the Mediterranean.
Arab armies brought Islam in 642 AD. Italy ruled Libya from 1911 until 1943. Libya became independent in 1951. Oil was found seven years later and changed everything.
wows: Libya has Africa's largest oil reserves (oil still underground), about 48 billion barrels.
Roman Leptis Magna lay buried in sand for 800 years, almost perfectly kept.
Waw an Namus volcano left a 20 km ash field with three salty crater lakes.
Over 90% of Libya is desert, one of Earth's highest shares.
Libya has Africa's longest Mediterranean coastline, at 1,770 km.
Ghadames has rooftop walkways so people could cross town above the street.
The Greek city of Cyrene, founded in 631 BC, still stands on a Libyan hillside.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: A camel's hump stores fat, not water. A thirsty camel can drink about 100 litres in a few minutes.

myths.myth: The Sahara is all rolling sand dunes
myths.fact: Most of the Sahara is flat gravel and bare rock. Sand dunes cover only about a quarter of it.
